description: Reason about time and space growth and use that model to improve data-intensive application code.

archetypes.name: Complexity-Aware Record Matching
archetypes.coreConcept: Estimate how work grows with input size, then trade additional memory for fewer repeated searches when matching records by a stable key.
mentalModel: Count how many times each input element is visited as the input grows.
A nested scan can compare each record against many records, producing quadratic growth.
Building a keyed index costs additional linear memory and setup work, then supports repeated constant-time average lookups.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Each record is indexed once and each matching record is emitted once in source order, with unmatched records excluded.

cognitiveTraps.name: Repeated Nested Search
cognitiveTraps.description: Keeping a full scan inside another full scan makes matching work grow roughly with the product of both collection sizes.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: For two collections with n records each, compare each left record against every right record; the number of comparisons grows near n squared.

cognitiveTraps.name: Ignoring the Index Memory Cost
cognitiveTraps.description: Claiming a faster lookup is free while omitting the auxiliary storage required to build the index.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Describe a keyed lookup as constant extra space even though a map retains one entry for each indexed record.

realWorldDomains.description: Matching shipment events to manifest entries using a shipment identifier while preserving event order.

qualityChecks.check: Repeated record matching reuses an index built from the lookup collection instead of rescanning that full collection for every input record.
qualityChecks.why: Reusing the index changes repeated matching work from quadratic growth to linear expected work while making the memory tradeoff explicit.

qualityChecks.check: Complexity explanations identify which input sizes drive the work and include auxiliary storage when an index is retained.
qualityChecks.why: A complexity label without its input dimensions or memory cost can hide the real scaling limit and tradeoff.

archetypes.name: Recursive Base-Case and Progress Trace
archetypes.coreConcept: A recursive function terminates when every reachable path reaches a base case, and each recursive step moves its input toward that case.
mentalModel: Write down the input for the current call before following its recursive call.
A base case returns without creating another frame.
A recursive case must make measurable progress toward a base case.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Every reachable recursive path decreases the remaining problem measure until a base case returns.

cognitiveTraps.name: Base Case Boundary Shift
cognitiveTraps.description: Stopping one call too early or too late changes the result or causes an extra recursive call.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A countdown intended to include zero returns at one, or recurses from zero to a negative value.

cognitiveTraps.name: No Progress Toward the Base Case
cognitiveTraps.description: A recursive call preserves or increases the measure needed to reach termination.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A recursive countdown calls itself with the same count when count is positive.

realWorldDomains.description: Tracing a bounded retry policy whose remaining-attempt count moves toward a stopping case.

qualityChecks.check: Each recursive path changes the relevant input measure toward a reachable base case.
qualityChecks.why: A call that does not make progress can recurse indefinitely or exceed the runtime stack.

qualityChecks.check: Base cases match the function's stated boundary contract and return without another recursive call.
qualityChecks.why: An off-by-one base case changes boundary behavior and may add an unnecessary frame.

archetypes.name: Call-Stack Frames and Return Unwinding
archetypes.coreConcept: Each recursive invocation has its own parameters and suspended return point; values combine or pass back as calls unwind.
mentalModel: Record each invocation as a distinct frame with its own argument values.
The deepest frame that reaches a base case returns first.
Resume suspended expressions from the deepest caller outward.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A caller resumes exactly once after its child returns, using that child's returned value in the suspended expression.

cognitiveTraps.name: Unwind Order Reversed
cognitiveTraps.description: Applying caller operations before the deepest call has returned.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: For total(n) = n + total(n - 1), add from the outermost frame downward instead of returning from the base case upward.

cognitiveTraps.name: Recursive Frames Treated as Shared State
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming each invocation overwrites the prior invocation's parameter or local value.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Treating local index values from nested calls as one mutable index rather than separate frame bindings.

cognitiveTraps.name: Sibling Calls Reuse a Prior Frame's State
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming a later independent recursive call begins with a local value left by an earlier sibling call.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A route-depth audit starts both region walks at depth zero, but a trace carries the first region's final depth into the second region.

realWorldDomains.description: Tracing recursive subtotal aggregation across nested invoice groups.

qualityChecks.check: Values belonging to separate recursive invocations remain distinguishable while tracing the call stack.
qualityChecks.why: Each invocation owns its own parameter and local bindings until its frame returns.

qualityChecks.check: Post-call work is evaluated only after the child invocation returns, in last-in-first-out order.
qualityChecks.why: The call stack suspends each caller until the nested call supplies its return value.

archetypes.name: Nested Structure Recursion Trace
archetypes.coreConcept: Recursive rules can decompose a nested structure into smaller child problems, with each leaf or empty structure providing a stopping condition.
mentalModel: At each frame, identify the current node and the children that create new calls.
Trace sibling calls in source order while keeping each branch's return separate.
Combine a node's local contribution with the results returned by its children.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Every recursive child is a strict substructure, and each node contributes exactly once to the final result.

cognitiveTraps.name: Empty Structure Lacks a Base Case
cognitiveTraps.description: The recursive rule attempts to inspect children when the current structure is empty.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A nested list traversal reads the first element without handling an empty list.

cognitiveTraps.name: A Branch Result Is Omitted
cognitiveTraps.description: One child result is not included when a recursive rule combines sibling branches.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A folder-size calculation visits subfolders but returns only the current folder's direct files.

realWorldDomains.description: Following recursive directory-size or quota calculations over nested folders.

qualityChecks.check: Each recursive child call receives a strictly smaller part of the current structure.
qualityChecks.why: Strictly smaller subproblems make structural progress toward an empty or leaf base case.

qualityChecks.check: The trace accounts for the local contribution and every required child result exactly once.
qualityChecks.why: Missing or duplicated branch results produce incorrect aggregates on nested data.

archetypes.name: Streaming Delimiter Validation
archetypes.coreConcept: A stack retains unmatched opening delimiters; each closer matches only the most recent opener, and valid input ends with no unmatched openers.
mentalModel: Scan left to right once.
Push opening delimiters because their closers are still expected.
Compare each closer with the most recent opener before removing it.
A mismatch fails immediately; an empty stack at the end completes the contract.
archetypes.governingInvariant: After each scanned character, the stack contains exactly the unmatched opening delimiters in original order.

cognitiveTraps.name: Delimiter Type Ignored
cognitiveTraps.description: Treating any closer as a match for any opener instead of checking the matching pair.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Input `([)]` has balanced counts but crossed delimiter types.

cognitiveTraps.name: Pop Before Checking the Stack
cognitiveTraps.description: Removing a stack item before proving one exists.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: An input beginning with `]` attempts to remove from an empty stack.

cognitiveTraps.name: Unclosed Opener Accepted
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning valid without checking for pending openers after the scan.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Input `((` ends with two unmatched openers.

realWorldDomains.description: Checking nested delimiters in a template before compilation.

qualityChecks.check: The retained state represents unmatched openers in order, and matching decisions use the most recent opener.
qualityChecks.why: Nested delimiters obey last-in-first-out order; counts cannot detect crossed pairs.

knownBad.code: return opens === closes;

qualityChecks.check: An unmatched closer is handled before removing an item, and remaining openers are checked after the scan.
qualityChecks.why: Empty-stack removal and accepting leftover openers both violate the contract.

knownBad.code: stack.pop(); return true;

qualityChecks.check: Each validation call owns its pending-delimiter state and does not retain it across calls.
qualityChecks.why: Shared state makes independent inputs depend on call order.

knownBad.code:
const pending = [];
function validate(source) { /* reuse pending */ }

archetypes.name: FIFO Job Buffer
archetypes.coreConcept: A queue admits work at the back and releases the oldest pending item from the front, preserving arrival order.
mentalModel: Enqueue adds after all items already waiting.
Dequeue removes the oldest waiting item.
An empty queue has no oldest item, so dequeue needs an explicit contract.
A head index can avoid shifting every remaining entry after removal.
archetypes.governingInvariant: The logical queue is exactly the not-yet-removed items in arrival order, independent of physical storage.

cognitiveTraps.name: Queue Uses Stack Order
cognitiveTraps.description: Removing the newest item rather than the oldest.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: After two different jobs are enqueued, the second is returned first.

cognitiveTraps.name: Front Removal Hides Repeated Work
cognitiveTraps.description: Repeated array shifting moves all remaining entries on every dequeue.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Draining n jobs with front shifts performs quadratic total element movement.

cognitiveTraps.name: Empty Dequeue Is Ambiguous
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning a valid payload value when no item exists.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: If `undefined` is a permitted payload, returning it for empty cannot signal absence.

realWorldDomains.description: Dispatching queued email jobs in accepted order.

qualityChecks.check: Removing pending work returns the oldest still-pending item and adding work keeps earlier items ahead.
qualityChecks.why: FIFO order prevents newer jobs from overtaking older jobs.

knownBad.code: return jobs.pop();

qualityChecks.check: The empty-queue outcome is distinguishable from every permitted queued payload.
qualityChecks.why: Callers must know whether an item was removed without confusing absence with valid data.

knownBad.code: function dequeue() { return undefined; }

qualityChecks.check: Queue storage is private, and removing the oldest item does not move every remaining item on each dequeue.
qualityChecks.why: Private state protects ordering invariants, while avoiding repeated suffix movement prevents quadratic work when draining a growing backlog.

knownBad.code: function dequeue() { return jobs.shift(); }

archetypes.name: Reusable Stack and Queue Contracts
archetypes.coreConcept: Collection modules are reliable when operations define empty behavior, preserve ordering, isolate state per instance, and hide storage details.
mentalModel: Define observable behavior before choosing a backing representation.
Use independent instances to check state isolation.
Exercise empty, singleton, repeated removal, and reuse after empty.
Keep callers on operations so representation changes cannot break their assumptions.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Each instance depends only on its own operation history and preserves its structure-specific ordering.

cognitiveTraps.name: Collection Instances Share State
cognitiveTraps.description: Backing storage is allocated at module scope and reused across instances.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Push into one stack and observe the item when popping from a new stack.

cognitiveTraps.name: Patch Only the Demonstrated Sequence
cognitiveTraps.description: Special-casing one observed operation sequence rather than preserving the general contract.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A queue passes two enqueues but fails after dequeue followed by enqueue.

cognitiveTraps.name: Arbitrary Capacity Boundary
cognitiveTraps.description: A fixed small capacity silently rejects or overwrites entries without contract support.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A collection loses data after an unexplained internal limit.

realWorldDomains.description: Independent queue instances for separate worker pools.

qualityChecks.check: Each instance owns independent mutable state, and callers cannot mutate its representation directly.
qualityChecks.why: Isolation prevents cross-request contamination while encapsulation keeps invariants enforceable.

knownBad.code:
let items = [];
function createStack() { return { push: (item) => items.push(item) }; }

qualityChecks.check: Public operations consistently implement empty and reuse boundary behavior.
qualityChecks.why: Boundary and lifecycle behavior is part of the API contract, not an incidental detail.

knownBad.code: function dequeue() { return items.shift() || null; }

qualityChecks.check: Callers use collection operations instead of depending on backing-array indexes or cleanup strategy.
qualityChecks.why: Hiding representation lets implementation changes preserve invariants.

knownBad.code: return { items, dequeue: () => items.shift() };

archetypes.name: Map Frequency Index
archetypes.coreConcept: A Map models frequency counts by preserving each exact key and associating it with a count that can be updated in place.
mentalModel: 1. Start with an empty keyed index.
2. Read the current count for each input key, treating only an absent entry as a new count.
3. Return the index after one pass through the input.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Every source key remains distinct according to the declared key contract, and its stored count equals the number of occurrences processed.

cognitiveTraps.name: Normalize Distinct Keys Without a Contract
cognitiveTraps.description: Lowercasing or otherwise transforming keys can merge values that the input contract treats as distinct.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function count(codes: readonly string[]): Map<string, number> { const out = new Map<string, number>(); for (const code of codes) out.set(code.toLowerCase(), (out.get(code.toLowerCase()) ?? 0) + 1); return out; }

cognitiveTraps.name: Treat Dynamic Keys Like Object Properties
cognitiveTraps.description: An object used as an index can collide with inherited names or special property behavior when the domain allows arbitrary keys.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const counts: Record<string, number> = {}; for (const key of keys) counts[key] = (counts[key] ?? 0) + 1;

realWorldDomains.description: Count exact event codes in an analytics window.
Aggregate repeated scan identifiers without coercing or normalizing the source keys.

archetypes.source: MDN Web Docs: Map — Key equality and keyed collections.

qualityChecks.check: Index keys retain the distinctions promised by the input contract; normalization is applied only when the prompt explicitly requests it.
qualityChecks.why: Unrequested normalization can merge distinct records and corrupt counts.

knownBad.code: function count(codes: readonly string[]): Map<string, number> { const result = new Map<string, number>(); for (const code of codes) result.set(code.toLowerCase(), (result.get(code.toLowerCase()) ?? 0) + 1); return result; }

qualityChecks.check: Each processed key has a count equal to its occurrence total, and the original input is not mutated.
qualityChecks.why: Incorrect initialization or updates silently lose telemetry.

knownBad.code: function count(codes: readonly string[]): Map<string, number> { const result = new Map<string, number>(); for (const code of codes) result.set(code, 1); return result; }

archetypes.name: Map Grouping and Key Identity
archetypes.coreConcept: Map supports grouping under values of any type; primitive keys follow SameValueZero and object keys follow reference identity.
mentalModel: 1. Identify which runtime value is the actual grouping key.
2. Check whether a bucket exists without treating valid falsy keys as absent.
3. Append each record to exactly the bucket selected by that key.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Each input record appears in one bucket selected by the exact key semantics named in the contract.

cognitiveTraps.name: Zero Is a Valid Key
cognitiveTraps.description: A truthiness check confuses the numeric key zero with an absent key.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: if (!accountId) return; // drops accountId 0

cognitiveTraps.name: Object Keys Are Compared by Reference
cognitiveTraps.description: Map does not merge distinct object references because their fields happen to look alike.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const first = { id: "A" }; const second = { id: "A" }; const map = new Map([[first, 1]]); map.get(second); // undefined

realWorldDomains.description: Group ledger entries by numeric account identifiers including zero.
Group tickets by the exact in-memory owner session object.

archetypes.source: MDN Web Docs: Map — Key equality and keyed collections.

qualityChecks.check: Every input record is placed in exactly one bucket selected by its declared key, including falsy primitive keys.
qualityChecks.why: Skipping a valid key loses records from the grouped result.

knownBad.code: function addGroup(groups: Map<number, string[]>, accountId: number, label: string): void { if (!accountId) return; groups.set(accountId, [...(groups.get(accountId) ?? []), label]); }

qualityChecks.check: When the contract names object references as keys, grouping uses reference identity rather than serialized or structural equality.
qualityChecks.why: Different runtime handles can represent distinct entities even when their fields match.

knownBad.code: function sameOwner(left: { id: string }, right: { id: string }): boolean { return left.id === right.id; }

archetypes.name: Set Stable Deduplication
archetypes.coreConcept: Set stores each SameValueZero-distinct value once and iterates the surviving values in first successful insertion order.
mentalModel: 1. Read values in source order.
2. Keep the first occurrence of each key under Set equality.
3. Return the retained values without sorting or mutating the input.
archetypes.governingInvariant: The output contains one copy of each distinct value in the order its first occurrence appeared.

cognitiveTraps.name: Set Deduplication Followed by Sorting
cognitiveTraps.description: Sorting the Set output discards the source order promised by a stable deduplication contract.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: return [...new Set(values)].sort();

cognitiveTraps.name: Structurally Similar Objects Are Distinct Set Values
cognitiveTraps.description: Distinct object references remain distinct even when their properties match.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: new Set([{ id: "A" }, { id: "A" }]).size // 2

realWorldDomains.description: Keep first-seen package aliases while removing repeated exact strings.
Preserve event arrival order while filtering repeated primitive IDs.

archetypes.source: MDN Web Docs: Set — Keyed collections and iteration order.

qualityChecks.check: Deduplicated output preserves the first-occurrence order required by the contract.
qualityChecks.why: Sorting or using a non-stable replacement changes downstream processing order.

knownBad.code: function unique(values: readonly string[]): string[] { return [...new Set(values)].sort(); }

qualityChecks.check: The source collection is not modified while building the unique result.
qualityChecks.why: Mutation can affect callers and later operations that reuse the input.

knownBad.code: function unique(values: string[]): string[] { values.sort(); return [...new Set(values)]; }

archetypes.name: Singly Linked List Boundary Mutations
archetypes.coreConcept: A singly linked list is a chain of nodes where each next reference identifies the successor and the list separately tracks its first and last nodes.
mentalModel: 1. Treat head, tail, size, and every next link as one shared invariant.
2. Identify whether a mutation changes the first node, last node, or an interior link.
3. Update every affected list field before returning.
archetypes.governingInvariant: An empty list has no head or tail; a non-empty list has both, its tail has no successor, and size equals the number of reachable nodes.

cognitiveTraps.name: Leave a Removed Tail Reachable
cognitiveTraps.description: Removing the final node can leave tail pointing at a node no longer reachable from head.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: if (current.next === null) { current = null; } // tail still points at removed node

cognitiveTraps.name: Miss an Empty-to-Singleton Transition
cognitiveTraps.description: Adding the first node must initialize both endpoints, not just head.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: if (this.head === null) this.head = node; else this.tail.next = node; this.tail = node;

realWorldDomains.description: Maintain an ordered queue of pending event records.
Apply ordered insertion and deletion in a registry mirror.

archetypes.source: TypeScript Handbook 5.9.3: strict null checking and narrowing; linked-list invariants are derived from the stated data-structure contract.

qualityChecks.check: Every mutation keeps head and tail consistent with reachability, including empty and singleton transitions.
qualityChecks.why: Stale endpoint references corrupt subsequent operations even when current output looks correct.

knownBad.code: if (this.head === null) this.head = node; else this.tail!.next = node; // tail never initialized

qualityChecks.check: The stored size equals the number of nodes reachable from head after each successful mutation.
qualityChecks.why: Incorrect counts make public length metadata diverge from the collection.

knownBad.code: removeFirst() { this.head = this.head?.next ?? null; } // size unchanged

qualityChecks.check: Mutations change only list-owned links and do not rewrite caller-owned values.
qualityChecks.why: Changing payload records as a side effect can corrupt other consumers.

knownBad.code: items[0].next = items[1]; return items;

archetypes.name: Doubly Linked List Link Symmetry
archetypes.coreConcept: A doubly linked list stores both predecessor and successor references, so each adjacent pair must agree in both directions.
mentalModel: 1. Locate the node and its left/right neighbors.
2. Reconnect the neighbors to each other in both directions.
3. Normalize head/tail links and size at the boundaries.
archetypes.governingInvariant: For every adjacent pair A and B, A.next is B exactly when B.previous is A; the head has no previous node and the tail has no next node.

cognitiveTraps.name: Update Only One Direction
cognitiveTraps.description: Changing next but not previous leaves reverse traversal connected to removed nodes.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: left.next = right; // right.previous still references removed

cognitiveTraps.name: Assume Both Neighbors Exist
cognitiveTraps.description: Head and tail removals have one missing neighbor and require endpoint updates.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: node.previous!.next = node.next!; node.next!.previous = node.previous!;

realWorldDomains.description: Maintain a bidirectional history sequence with fast endpoint updates.
Move or remove adjacent media items while supporting reverse navigation.

archetypes.source: TypeScript Handbook 5.9.3: strict null checking and narrowing; bidirectional links are governed by the collection contract.

qualityChecks.check: Every reconnect updates both neighboring references so forward and backward traversal describe the same sequence.
qualityChecks.why: One-sided changes produce inconsistent iteration and retain detached nodes.

knownBad.code: left.next = right; // missing reciprocal previous update

qualityChecks.check: Boundary operations handle a missing predecessor or successor without unsafe dereferences and update the matching endpoint.
qualityChecks.why: The first and last nodes do not have two neighbors.

knownBad.code: node.previous!.next = node.next!; node.next!.previous = node.previous!;

qualityChecks.check: A removed node is no longer reachable from either endpoint and does not retain active neighbor links.
qualityChecks.why: Detached nodes retaining links can expose stale collection state.

knownBad.code: left.next = right; right.previous = left; // removed node still links to both

archetypes.name: Linked List Mutation Regression
archetypes.coreConcept: Linked-list mutation defects often appear only after a sequence crosses an endpoint boundary, so checks must reason over transitions rather than isolated calls.
mentalModel: 1. Replay the operation sequence from the initial state.
2. Compare reachable nodes, endpoints, and size after every step.
3. Add a regression case for the boundary transition that exposes the divergence.
archetypes.governingInvariant: After every operation the sequence from head and the reverse sequence from tail agree with the same set of active nodes and the reported size.

cognitiveTraps.name: Test Only the Immediate Return Value
cognitiveTraps.description: A mutation may appear correct before a later append or reverse traversal exposes a stale link.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: removeTail(); append(next); // stale tail can make the new node unreachable

cognitiveTraps.name: Remove a Different Equal-Payload Node
cognitiveTraps.description: When the contract identifies a node or position, comparing payloads can unlink a different node with an equal value.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: if (cursor.value === target.value) unlink(cursor);

cognitiveTraps.name: Retain a Tail After the List Is Empty
cognitiveTraps.description: Clearing the last reachable node without clearing the tail leaves a stale endpoint that can disconnect a later append.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: this.head = null; // tail still refers to the removed node

realWorldDomains.description: Keep queued work ordered as items are removed and reinserted.
Keep back/forward navigation consistent through endpoint changes.

archetypes.source: TypeScript Handbook 5.9.3: strict null checking and narrowing; mutation-sequence tests follow the declared linked-list contract.

qualityChecks.check: After any successful removal, head, tail, and size agree with the active linked nodes before the method returns.
qualityChecks.why: A stale endpoint can make later operations disconnect active nodes even when the immediate return value looks correct.

knownBad.code: if (this.head === removed) { this.head = null; this.count -= 1; return removed.value; }

qualityChecks.check: All active nodes are reachable exactly once from the declared head and reverse traversal reaches the same sequence from tail.
qualityChecks.why: Cycles, detached nodes, and stale endpoints can hide behind correct payload output.

knownBad.code: tail.next = head; // accidentally creates a cycle

archetypes.name: Depth-First Preorder Traversal
archetypes.coreConcept: Depth-first preorder visits a node before its descendants and follows the declared child order for each subtree.
mentalModel: 1. Start at the root and record its value.
2. Visit each child subtree completely before moving to the next sibling.
3. An absent root produces an empty result.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Each reachable tree node is included exactly once, before all of its descendants, with sibling order preserved.

cognitiveTraps.name: Reverse Siblings with a LIFO Worklist
cognitiveTraps.description: Pushing children in their listed order onto a stack makes the last child leave first.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: for (const child of node.children) stack.push(child); // later pop visits siblings in reverse order

cognitiveTraps.name: Record Only Descendants
cognitiveTraps.description: A preorder walk records the node after or instead of its children.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: for (const child of node.children) visit(child); output.push(node.value);

realWorldDomains.description: Collect nested folder labels in documented display order.
Enumerate a category tree for a stable navigation menu.

archetypes.source: TypeScript Handbook 5.9.3: recursive generic types and strict null checks; traversal order follows the declared tree contract.

qualityChecks.check: Traversal includes a node before its descendants and preserves each node’s declared child order.
qualityChecks.why: Changing hierarchy order changes display, processing, or reporting semantics.

knownBad.code: for (const child of node.children) stack.push(child); while (stack.length) visit(stack.pop()!);

qualityChecks.check: Every reachable node appears exactly once, including leaves and the root.
qualityChecks.why: Skipping a boundary node or visiting a shared child twice corrupts aggregates.

knownBad.code: output.push(node.value); for (const child of node.children.slice(1)) visit(child);

qualityChecks.check: Traversal leaves caller-owned child arrays and node values unchanged.
qualityChecks.why: Mutating input trees affects other consumers and later traversals.

knownBad.code: node.children.reverse();

archetypes.name: Breadth-First Level Grouping
archetypes.coreConcept: Breadth-first traversal processes all nodes at one depth before any node at the next depth.
mentalModel: 1. Put the root into a first-in, first-out worklist.
2. Capture the current worklist width as the number of nodes at this depth.
3. Process that many nodes, appending their children for the next depth.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Each level group contains exactly the nodes at that depth in left-to-right child order, and each node is enqueued and processed once.

cognitiveTraps.name: Mix Nodes from Adjacent Levels
cognitiveTraps.description: Using a queue length that changes during the level loop can consume newly queued children too early.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: for (let i = 0; i < queue.length; i += 1) { const node = queue.shift(); queue.push(...node.children); }

cognitiveTraps.name: Lose Linear Traversal Work
cognitiveTraps.description: Removing the first item by shifting the remaining queue repeatedly adds avoidable work.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: while (queue.length) { const node = queue.shift(); visit(node); }

realWorldDomains.description: Group an organizational hierarchy by reporting depth.
Build category navigation sections by hierarchy depth.

archetypes.source: TypeScript Handbook 5.9.3: recursive generic types and strict null checks; breadth-first ordering follows the stated level contract.

qualityChecks.check: Each output group contains only nodes at the same depth and groups appear from shallowest to deepest.
qualityChecks.why: Mixing queue generations produces misleading hierarchy summaries.

knownBad.code: while (queue.length) { const node = queue[head++]; current.push(node.value); for (const child of node.children) queue.push(child); }

qualityChecks.check: Nodes at the same depth retain the declared sibling order.
qualityChecks.why: Stable order keeps navigation and reports predictable.

knownBad.code: for (const child of node.children.slice().reverse()) queue.push(child);

qualityChecks.check: Each node is added to and removed from the worklist a bounded number of times.
qualityChecks.why: Repeatedly shifting the remaining queue can make a wide traversal quadratic.

knownBad.code: while (queue.length) { const item = queue.shift(); process(item); }

archetypes.name: Tree Search and Aggregate
archetypes.coreConcept: A tree query can stop at a matching node or combine child results while preserving traversal semantics and empty-tree behavior.
mentalModel: 1. Define the result for an absent root.
2. Visit each relevant node using the requested order.
3. Stop or aggregate only when the contract says to do so.
archetypes.governingInvariant: The result is derived from exactly the nodes permitted by the query contract, and a search returns the first matching node in traversal order.

cognitiveTraps.name: Return a Later Match
cognitiveTraps.description: A search contract for the first match requires stopping when the earliest traversal match is found.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: if (node.id === target) found = node; // descendants can overwrite the first match

cognitiveTraps.name: Use a Non-Identity Empty Result
cognitiveTraps.description: An empty tree must produce the neutral value named by its contract.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: return root === null ? 1 : count(root);

realWorldDomains.description: Find the first matching policy group along a documented traversal order.
Aggregate counts across nested catalog categories.

archetypes.source: TypeScript Handbook 5.9.3: recursive generic types and strict null checks; search and aggregate behavior follow the declared contract.

qualityChecks.check: A first-match search returns the earliest matching node under the declared traversal order.
qualityChecks.why: Overwriting a match later in the walk silently changes which policy or record is selected.

archetypes.name: BFS Shortest Unweighted Path
archetypes.coreConcept: Breadth-first search explores vertices in non-decreasing hop distance from the start node, marking neighbors visited on enqueue so each vertex enters the queue at most once.
mentalModel: Check missing start/target vertices and the start === target trivial path first.
Mark neighbors visited when enqueuing them rather than when dequeuing.
Advance a queue head index instead of calling Array.prototype.shift().
archetypes.governingInvariant: Every vertex is enqueued at most once and its recorded parent/distance matches a minimum-hop path from start.

cognitiveTraps.name: Mark Visited Only on Dequeue
cognitiveTraps.description: Deferring visited marking until dequeue lets multiple parents enqueue the same node and can overwrite parent pointers.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const current = queue[head++]; if (visited.has(current)) continue; visited.add(current);

cognitiveTraps.name: Missing Start-Equals-Target Guard
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning null or requiring at least one edge when start equals target produces wrong hop counts.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: if (next === target) return hops; // never checked before loop when start === target

realWorldDomains.description: Compute minimum-hop service-to-service routes across unweighted microservice links.

archetypes.source: MDN JavaScript Guide (Map/Set) & standard unweighted BFS shortest-path algorithm.

qualityChecks.check: BFS marks start and newly discovered neighbors visited when adding them to the queue rather than after dequeuing.
qualityChecks.why: Marking at enqueue time prevents duplicate queue entries and guarantees minimum-hop parent pointers.

qualityChecks.check: BFS advances a queue head index (or O(1) queue) instead of calling Array.prototype.shift() in the traversal loop.
qualityChecks.why: Repeated shift() re-indexes the queue array and turns an O(V + E) traversal into quadratic work.

archetypes.name: Three-State Directed Cycle Detection
archetypes.coreConcept: A directed graph contains a cycle if and only if depth-first search traverses an edge into a vertex currently on the active recursion stack (visiting), not merely an already-finished vertex (visited).
mentalModel: Track three states per vertex: unvisited, visiting (active stack), and visited (completed).
Iterate over every vertex in the graph so disconnected components are checked.
Handle self-loops (u -> u) as immediate back-edges to a visiting vertex.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A cycle is reported if and only if a directed path leads from a vertex back to itself.

cognitiveTraps.name: Binary Visited Set Flags DAG Diamond
cognitiveTraps.description: Using a single boolean visited set treats converging branches in a DAG as a cycle.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: if (visited.has(next)) return true; // fails on A -> B -> D and A -> C -> D

cognitiveTraps.name: Single-Start Misses Disconnected Component
cognitiveTraps.description: Starting DFS from only the first node misses cycles in other components.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: return dfs(nodes[0]); // skips unreachable component containing a cycle

realWorldDomains.description: Detect circular task or package dependencies in a workspace build graph.

archetypes.source: MDN JavaScript Guide & TypeScript Handbook 5.9.3: 3-color DFS state discrimination.

qualityChecks.check: Directed cycle detection separates active stack vertices (visiting) from completed vertices (visited) and checks all graph components.
qualityChecks.why: A two-state visited set reports false cycles on valid DAG diamonds, while single-start DFS misses disconnected cycles.

knownBad.code: if (visited.has(next)) return true;

qualityChecks.check: Graph utilities do not mutate caller-provided edge lists or adjacency maps.
qualityChecks.why: Mutating shared graph inputs corrupts downstream queries and violates caller ownership.

knownBad.code: edges.sort((a, b) => a[0].localeCompare(b[0]));

archetypes.name: Graph Reachability & Component Queries
archetypes.coreConcept: Adjacency Map representations and BFS/DFS reachability queries decouple graph indexing from traversal so callers can inspect reachable sets, components, or valid topological steps in O(V + E).
mentalModel: Build adjacency Map and in-degree counts in one pass without mutating inputs.
Use Set for visited membership and head-index queue for BFS expansion.
Return explicit empty or null results when nodes are unknown or cycles block ordering.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Every reachable vertex or zero-in-degree stage is emitted at most once in valid dependency order, or failure is signaled explicitly on cycles.

cognitiveTraps.name: Confusing Directed and Undirected Edges
cognitiveTraps.description: Adding reverse edges on a directed dependency graph or omitting reverse edges on an undirected route breaks reachability.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: graph.get(to).push(from); // added reverse edge on a directed dependency graph

cognitiveTraps.name: Mutating Caller Graph Inputs
cognitiveTraps.description: Sorting or popping caller-owned edge arrays or neighbor arrays mutates caller state.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const next = graph.get(node).pop();

archetypes.source: MDN JavaScript Guide & TypeScript Handbook 5.9.3: Map/Set graph traversal invariants.

qualityChecks.check: Directed graph builders and reachability queries preserve edge direction instead of inserting reverse edges.
qualityChecks.why: Adding reverse edges turns directed dependency queries into undirected reachability and produces invalid impact sets.

knownBad.code: adjacency.get(to)?.push(from);

qualityChecks.check: Graph queries build local Map/Set indexes without mutating caller-owned edge lists or neighbor arrays.
qualityChecks.why: Preserves caller data across repeated graph queries.
